claims.text: Percolation of SRO clusters in single-phase bcc refractory high-entropy alloys causes a non-monotonic transition from reduced to enhanced thermal conductivity.
Connected chemically ordered pathways bypass lattice-distortion scattering in the high-entropy matrix.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a single-phase bcc random solid solution or low-density-SRO state.
Sintered HfNbTaTiZr has a thermal conductivity of approximately 10–17 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.
Lattice distortion and defects such as grain boundaries and dislocations suppress electron and phonon propagation in HfNbTaTiZr.
Annealing just below the order-disorder transition temperature allows SRO clusters to grow and become connected.
The annealing treatment should preserve a single phase and avoid secondary phases such as Laves phases.
The range 0.5–0.8 T_m contains a regime in which SRO clusters percolate without dissolving.
Irradiation near or above the ODTT homogenizes chemical distributions and drives SRO parameters toward zero in W-Ta-Cr-V-Hf alloys.
Stress-free testing isolates phonon transport from dislocation-mediated effects.
Percolating SRO clusters have lower lattice distortion than the random matrix and form continuous low-scattering phonon highways.
Isolated SRO clusters act as scattering centers and increase thermal resistivity.
SRO percolation creates a connected sublattice with reduced effective mass fluctuation and a lower phonon-scattering potential.
SRO flattens the energy landscape for edge dislocations and lowers solute drag in bcc MoNbTaW.
The edge-dislocation energy-landscape mechanism in MoNbTaW is analogous to enhanced phonon propagation through SRO pathways.
Thermal conductivity should show an inflection and increase, potentially above the random-solid-solution baseline, after the SRO volume fraction crosses a percolation threshold.
Standard serial or parallel mixing models predict a monotonic decrease in thermal conductivity as SRO increases.
The proposed effect disappears when SRO remains isolated, phase decomposition occurs, or temperatures reach the ODTT and homogenize the alloy.
The SRO percolation threshold and conductivity increase depend on specific pair-interaction energies in the target alloy.
SRO-induced strengthening may alter dislocation behavior and introduce secondary phonon-scattering mechanisms.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome says conductivity only potentially exceeds the random-solid-solution baseline, whereas the falsification rule treats remaining below that baseline as decisive falsification even if conductivity rises after percolation. Thus baseline exceedance is optional in the prediction but mandatory in the falsification criterion.
